title: Doomsday eyes $270M-plus opening as Dune 3 targets $75M
excerpt:
New details have emerged about the project.
The report separates confirmed information from editorial context.
body_md:
Early audience tracking has placed two major December releases at the center of an unusually competitive theatrical weekend. Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday, directed by Joe and Anthony Russo, has entered National Research Group tracking with a projected North American opening of more than $270 million. Dune: Part Three is meanwhile tracking toward a debut of approximately $75 million.

The Avengers figure represents the highest initial projection reported in NRG's tracking history. That distinction concerns a forecast, not an actual box office record. The film has yet to open, and estimates can change substantially as marketing campaigns progress and audience intentions translate into ticket purchases.

For comparison, the report available in the feed says Spider-Man: Brand New Day entered tracking at $180 million before ultimately achieving a $360 million domestic opening. That difference illustrates why an early projection should not be mistaken for a fixed ceiling or a guaranteed result.

If Doomsday reaches its current forecast, it would exceed the $260 million December 2021 opening of Spider-Man: No Way Home. It would also surpass Disney's previous December benchmark of $247.9 million, established by Star Wars: The Force Awakens. A debut above $300 million has been discussed as a possibility, but the initial tracking does not establish that outcome.

Audience interest appears particularly strong among men younger than 25, with men aged 25 and older following closely behind. First-choice indicators are useful because they measure relative preference among available entertainment options, although they cannot guarantee attendance.

The timing immediately before Christmas introduces additional uncertainty. Winter weather, holiday travel and family commitments can influence when audiences choose to visit theaters. These factors are among the reasons analysts may hesitate to raise their forecasts before more information becomes available.

Dune: Part Three has its own substantial audience, and the report suggests an opening above $80 million would not be surprising. From an editorial perspective, simultaneous demand for two major releases could benefit the overall theatrical market, while also creating competition for premium screens and desirable showtimes.

Both films are scheduled to open on December 18, 2026. Adding their initial projections produces a combined figure of roughly $345 million before accounting for other titles. That arithmetic is not a separate industry forecast, and the final weekend total could differ considerably. The actual results will become clear only after audiences have had the opportunity to see both films.
